authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The Partnership and OpCo each amended their senior unsecured revolving credit agreements with Westlake, extending the maturities to July 2031.
The board of the general partner approved a third-quarter 2026 distribution of $0.4714 per common unit, payable December 1, 2026. It is described as the 49th consecutive quarterly distribution.
OpCo and Westlake renewed the Ethylene Sales Agreement, and also the Feedstock Supply Agreement, through December 31, 2027. This is a renewal, not a loss of the contract.
no_value_reason: minority interests take too large a share of income

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section and the MD&A overview.
business_model.claim: The Partnership is a holding vehicle. Its only revenue-generating asset is a 22.8% limited partner interest in OpCo, which it controls through ownership of OpCo's general partner.
quotes: Our sole revenue generating asset is our 22.8% limited partner interest in OpCo.

business_model.basis: Ownership is stated in the 10-K. The split is read from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Westlake holds the other 77.2% of OpCo, so most consolidated profit is attributed to the noncontrolling interest. In the latest nine months, net income was 254,874 (table in thousands of dollars). 210,248 went to the noncontrolling interest and 44,626 to the Partnership.
quotes: Westlake held a 77.2% limited partner interest in OpCo

business_model.claim: OpCo sells ethylene and co-products. It has three ethylene plants with aggregate annual capacity of about 3.7 billion pounds, plus an ethylene pipeline. Co-products include propylene, crude butadiene, pyrolysis gasoline and hydrogen.
quotes: OpCo's assets are comprised of three ethylene production facilities, which primarily convert ethane into ethylene and have an aggregate annual capacity of approximately 3.7 billion pounds, and a 200-mile ethylene pipeline.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and MD&A sections.
business_model.claim: The main customer is Westlake, its parent. Under the Ethylene Sales Agreement it buys 95% of OpCo's planned ethylene production on a cost-plus basis with a fixed margin of $0.10 per pound.
quotes: on a cost-plus basis that is expected to generate a fixed margin per pound of $0.10

business_model.basis: Read directly from the income statement and the MD&A results table. The F2 row labels for these lines are scrambled, so the split uses the P4 labels.
business_model.claim: In the latest nine months, sales to Westlake were 763,056, third-party sales were 154,178, and total net sales were 917,234 (table in thousands of dollars). A year earlier the figures were 736,396, 107,250 and 843,646. Westlake is the dominant buyer, and third-party sales are the faster-growing part.

business_model.basis: The share is stated in the 10-K. The quarterly figures come from the 10-Q. The price comment is in the Q2 release. The causal link to the Q3 increase is inferred, not stated.
business_model.claim: Third-party sales are the part exposed to market prices. They are the roughly 5% of output not sold to Westlake, plus co-products. They were 11.4% of total revenues in the prior fiscal year. In the latest quarter they were 52,524 against 32,359 a year earlier (table in thousands of dollars), and management cited higher third-party ethylene prices in the prior quarter.
quotes: During 2025, all third-party ethylene and associated co-products sales generated 11.4% of our total revenues.
we benefited from higher third-party ethylene prices

business_model.claim: The Partnership reports a single reportable segment, and all assets and operations are in the United States.
quotes: Our assets and operations are organized into a single reportable segment and are all located and conducted in the United States.

business_model.basis: Agreement terms are stated in the 10-K. The mechanism is the cost-plus design described there.
business_model.claim: Feedstock is a main cost and comes from Westlake. Under the Feedstock Supply Agreement, ethane is priced off a Mont Belvieu spot index plus transport and storage. The sales price adjusts for feedstock cost changes, which is how the $0.10 per pound margin is kept.
quotes: The price at which ethane and feedstock is sold includes an indexed price for spot gas liquids at Mont Belvieu and applicable transportation, storage and other costs.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and risk factors.
business_model.claim: Volume and plant outages drive results. In the prior fiscal year the Petro 1 turnaround cut volumes, which reduced net sales by 8.2%. The gross margin fell to 29.8% from 36.9% on higher ethane and natural gas costs. A Buyer Deficiency Fee of $5.8 million partly offset this.
quotes: Lower sales volumes in 2025 contributed to an 8.2% decrease in net sales compared to 2024.
The gross profit margin was 29.8% in 2025 as compared to 36.9% in 2024.

business_model.basis: Read directly from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Cost of sales is the largest cost. In the latest nine months it was 624,774 against sales of 917,234, leaving gross profit of 292,460 (table in thousands of dollars). Selling, general and administrative expense was 23,020. Gross profit was 251,036 a year earlier.

business_model.basis: The statement is in the 10-K risk factors. The amounts come from the 10-Q statements.
business_model.claim: Debt and public-partnership costs are not passed through to Westlake and reduce profit. Interest expense to Westlake was 15,314 in the latest nine months (table in thousands of dollars). Long-term debt payable to Westlake was 399,674.
quotes: The ethylene sales price also does not increase to cover our cost of debt or public partnership costs.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section and risk factors.
business_model.claim: Revenue depends heavily on a single related-party counterparty. The agreement was renewed through December 31, 2027, and either party can end it at the end of a term on at least 12 months' notice.
quotes: On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the Q3 earnings release.
business_model.claim: The Partnership's cash comes from OpCo distributions and is paid out as unitholder distributions. A quarterly distribution of $0.4714 per unit was declared for Q3. Trailing twelve-month coverage by MLP distributable cash flow was 1.09x.
quotes: Currently, all of our cash flow is generated from cash distributions from OpCo
MLP distributable cash flow provided trailing twelve-month coverage that was 1.09x the declared distributions for the third quarter of 2026

business_model.basis: The agreement is stated in the 10-K. The balances and flows come from the 10-Q statements.
business_model.claim: Excess cash is invested with Westlake under an Investment Management Agreement, which earns interest income. The receivable under it was 65,715 at the latest balance sheet date, after 42,000 of new investments in the nine months (table in thousands of dollars).
quotes: authorizes Westlake to invest the Partnership's and OpCo's excess cash with Westlake for durations of up to a maximum of nine months

competitive_position.claim: The Partnership has no independent operating business. Its sole revenue-generating asset is a 22.8% limited partner interest in OpCo, which it controls through OpCo's general partner. Westlake holds the other 77.2% of OpCo.
quotes: Our sole revenue generating asset is our 22.8% limited partner interest in OpCo.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 8-K earnings release and the 10-K Item 1.
competitive_position.claim: The main support for the competitive position is a long-term cost-plus ethylene sales contract with Westlake. Westlake buys 95% of OpCo's ethylene for a $0.10 per pound margin. In October 2025 the contract and the feedstock supply agreement were renewed through December 31, 2027.
quotes: The agreement provides that 95% of OpCo's ethylene production is sold to Westlake for a cash margin of $0.10 per pound, net of operating costs, maintenance capital expenditures and reserves for future turnaround expenditures.
On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.

competitive_position.claim: OpCo's physical base is three ethylene plants with about 3.7 billion pounds of annual capacity, plus a 200-mile ethylene pipeline. The plants are integrated with Westlake's downstream polyethylene and PVC operations, which consume most of the output.
quotes: OpCo's assets are comprised of three ethylene production facilities, which primarily convert ethane into ethylene and have an aggregate annual capacity of approximately 3.7 billion pounds, and a 200-mile ethylene pipeline.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement. The turnaround context is from the FY2025 10-K MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Operating results for the first nine months of 2026 were higher than a year earlier. Net sales and gross profit both rose.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement (table in thousands) and the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Earnings attributable to the Partnership also rose. Third-quarter net income attributable was 16,219 against 14,653, and the nine-month figure was 44,626 against 34,159.

Cash coverage of the distribution is positive but thin. Trailing twelve-month coverage was 1.09x for the third-quarter distribution of $0.4714 per unit, up from 1.04x at the end of the second quarter. Cumulative coverage since the IPO is about 1.05x.
quotes: MLP distributable cash flow provided trailing twelve-month coverage that was 1.09x the declared distributions for the third quarter of 2026, which was above the trailing twelve-month coverage ratio of 1.04x at the end of the second quarter.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors. The balances are from the 10-Q balance sheet.
competitive_position.claim: The largest threat named is dependence on a single counterparty, Westlake. All of the Partnership's cash comes from OpCo, and most of OpCo's cash comes from Westlake under the sales agreement. Westlake has pledged no security.
quotes: We are substantially dependent on Westlake for our cash flows.
Westlake has not pledged any assets to us as security for the performance of its obligations.

competitive_position.claim: The fixed-margin contract limits upside. The price does not rise to cover the Partnership's debt cost or public partnership costs, and the $0.10 per pound margin limits OpCo's ability to benefit from favorable markets.
quotes: The ethylene sales price also does not increase to cover our cost of debt or public partnership costs.

competitive_position.claim: Margins in percentage terms still moved with feedstock costs in 2025. Gross margin fell to 29.8% from 36.9% on higher ethane and natural gas costs. This shows the Partnership is not fully shielded from input-cost swings.
quotes: The decreased gross profit margin in 2025 was primarily due to higher ethane feedstock and natural gas costs in 2025 as compared to 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and Item 1.
competitive_position.claim: The agreements with Westlake are time-limited, so renewal is a named threat. If OpCo cannot extend or replace them, distributions could be materially adversely affected.
quotes: If OpCo were unable to reach agreement with Westlake on an extension or replacement of these agreements in the future, then our ability to make distributions on our common units could be materially adversely affected and the value of our common units could decline.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and Item 1.
competitive_position.claim: Operational concentration is a named threat. Substantially all of OpCo's sales come from three facilities at two sites, and OpCo relies on Westlake for services, labor and the leased land.
quotes: Substantially all of OpCo's sales are generated at three facilities located at two sites.
OpCo depends upon Westlake for numerous services and for its labor force.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A, the 10-Q income statement and the Q2 earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Merchant (third-party) sales are a small but growing source of commodity exposure. Management limits direct commodity price exposure to about 5% of ethylene production plus co-products. Third-party sales rose to 52,524 in the quarter from 32,359, and to 154,178 for nine months from 107,250.
quotes: our direct exposure to commodity price risk is limited to approximately 5% of our total ethylene production
we benefited from higher third-party ethylene prices

competitive_position.claim: Industry-level threats named in the risk factors include new ethylene capacity and cheaper naphtha-based competition. The 10-K lists increased ethylene production from recent capacity expansions among the market changes that could affect results. It also cites lower crude oil prices as eroding the advantage of ethane-based producers.
quotes: increased production of ethylene (a number of new ethylene capacity expansions have been recently completed)

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The variable-rate risk is from the 10-K risk factor summary.
competitive_position.claim: Financing terms are in place. In July 2026 the OpCo and Partnership revolvers were extended to July 11, 2031, which reduces near-term refinancing risk. The revolvers carry variable SOFR-based interest rates.
quotes: The OpCo Revolver Amendment extended the maturity date of the OpCo Revolver to July 11, 2031

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the comparison is a reading of the printed lines.
financial_health.claim: Cash and cash equivalents were 47,649 (table in thousands) at the latest balance sheet date, up from 44,269 at the prior year-end. Total current assets of 184,470 compare with total current liabilities of 52,451.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet, cash flow statement and 10-K business section.
financial_health.claim: Surplus cash is placed with Westlake under the Investment Management Agreement. The receivable under that agreement rose to 65,715 from 23,378, and 42,000 was invested in the nine months. The 10-K says Westlake provides daily availability of this cash.
quotes: Westlake provides daily availability of the invested cash to meet any liquidity needs of the Partnership or OpCo

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the interpretation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Debt is a single line, long-term debt payable to Westlake of 399,674, unchanged from year-end. Total liabilities are 454,919 against total equity of 770,285.
quotes: Long-term debt payable to Westlake | 399,674 | 399,674

financial_health.basis: Figures stated in the income statement; the rate sensitivity is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
financial_health.claim: Interest expense to Westlake was 15,314 for the nine months versus 17,391 a year earlier, against income from operations of 269,440. The 10-K flags that the variable-rate debt exposes the company to rising rates.
quotes: Our variable-rate debt exposes us to increases in interest rates, which could have a material impact on our financial position, results of operation and cash flows

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; the mechanism is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was 362,205 for the nine months versus 160,090 a year earlier. Additions to property, plant and equipment fell to 29,724 from 69,988, and depreciation and amortization was 101,531.

financial_health.basis: Figures and quote are stated; linking the 2025 deferred-charges outflow to the turnaround is inferred from the 10-K's comment on turnaround cash use.
financial_health.claim: The jump in operating cash flow is partly a base effect and a working-capital swing. Net receivables from Westlake were a source of 20,005 versus a use of (38,532), and deferred charges and other assets were 2,478 versus (123,817). The company said the third-quarter increase was primarily due to more favorable working capital changes.
quotes: primarily due to more favorable changes in working capital

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release; MLP distributable cash flow is a non-GAAP measure.
financial_health.claim: At the partnership level, cash available for distribution roughly covers payouts. MLP distributable cash flow was $53,500 (table in thousands) for the nine months against total distributions declared of $49,848. Trailing twelve-month coverage was 1.09x.
quotes: MLP distributable cash flow provided trailing twelve-month coverage that was 1.09x the declared distributions for the third quarter of 2026

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; the interpretation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Much of the consolidated cash goes to Westlake. Distributions to the noncontrolling interest in OpCo were 237,253 versus 180,645 a year earlier. Net cash used for financing was 287,101, and cash still rose by 3,380.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A recent developments and the August earnings release.
financial_health.claim: The revolving credit agreements were extended to July 11, 2031, which pushes out the main refinancing date. The OpCo revolver margin is 1.75%, and the MLP revolver margin varies between 1.75% and 2.75% with the Partnership's leverage ratio. The 0.10% credit spread adjustment was removed.
quotes: The OpCo Revolver Amendment extended the maturity date of the OpCo Revolver to July 11, 2031
The Applicable Margin under the OpCo Revolver is 1.75%.

financial_health.basis: Cash flow figures are stated; the absence of a current portion is inferred from the line labels.
financial_health.claim: Revolver borrowings and repayments to Westlake were both 124,500 in the nine months, so net debt was unchanged at 399,674. The balance sheet labels that debt long-term, and the evidence shows no current debt maturity on the balance sheet lines provided.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and risk factor sections; the concentration point is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The lender and the main customer are the same party, Westlake. The Ethylene Sales Agreement and Feedstock Supply Agreement were renewed through December 31, 2027. This supports cash flow visibility, but the risk factors say debt service competes with distributions.
quotes: On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.
Cash that is used to service debt will be unavailable for distributions to our unitholders.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated: the Q2 release attributes the gains to higher production and sales volume after the prior-year turnaround. The nine-month comparison is read from the income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Volume recovery after the 2025 Petro 1 turnaround is the main driver visible in the 2026 results. Nine-month total net sales were $917,234 (table in thousands) against $843,646, and net income attributable to the Partnership was $44,626 against $34,159.
quotes: primarily due to higher production and sales volume and lower maintenance capital expenditures as the result of the prior year's Petro 1 turnaround

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors; applying it to the 2026 volume gain is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: For this volume gain to continue, OpCo's plants must keep running without a major outage. Turnarounds are expected only about every five to eight years, and Westlake's purchase obligation can be suspended while facilities are not operating.
quotes: We expect that each of OpCo's facilities will have a turnaround approximately once every five to eight years and will not operate for typically between 30 and 60 days during each separate turnaround.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release and its reconciliation table.
growth_thesis.claim: Lower maintenance capital spending lifted MLP distributable cash flow. Nine-month maintenance capital expenditures were $34,887 (table in thousands) against $65,233, and MLP distributable cash flow was $53,500 against $34,607.
quotes: The increase in MLP distributable cash flow and associated trailing twelve-month coverage ratio of 1.09x was primarily due to lower maintenance capital expenditures and higher sales volume.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated: the Q2 release cites higher third-party prices. The third-party sales figures are read from the income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Third-party ethylene and co-product sales are a second source of growth. Nine-month third-party sales were $154,178 (table in thousands) against $107,250, and Q3 was $52,524 against $32,359.
quotes: we benefited from higher third-party ethylene prices

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section and risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The renewed Ethylene Sales Agreement with Westlake underpins the earnings base. It was renewed through December 31, 2027, with a fixed margin of $0.10 per pound. Continued growth requires Westlake to keep paying and the agreements to keep being renewed.
quotes: On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.
We are substantially dependent on Westlake for our cash flows.

growth_thesis.basis: The interest figures and the amendment are stated. The link to rates is inferred from the 10-K discussion of 2025.
growth_thesis.claim: Lower interest expense on debt to Westlake adds a smaller lift. Nine-month interest expense was $15,314 (table in thousands) against $17,391, and the July 2026 revolver amendments removed a 0.10% credit spread adjustment.
quotes: removed the 0.10% credit spread adjustment that had previously applied to the OpCo Revolver's Secured Overnight Financing Rate

growth_thesis.basis: The capacity statement and the list of levers are stated in the 10-K. Treating them as conditions for growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Further volume growth is limited by capacity. OpCo's plants already run close to full capacity, and Westlake has first call on most output, so growth beyond the recovery needs expansion, more ownership of OpCo, acquisitions or a higher fixed margin.
quotes: OpCo's ability to increase throughput volumes through its assets is constrained by the capacity limitations of those assets, which are currently operating at close to full capacity.
Our sole revenue generating asset is our 22.8% limited partner interest in OpCo.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release. The conclusion about payout growth is inferred from the flat declared amounts.
growth_thesis.claim: Earnings growth has not yet become distribution growth. The declared distribution is unchanged at $0.4714 per unit, and trailing twelve-month coverage rose to 1.09x.
quotes: MLP distributable cash flow provided trailing twelve-month coverage that was 1.09x the declared distributions for the third quarter of 2026

material_events.basis: stated in the cited items (8-K release and 10-Q MD&A)
material_events.claim: The Partnership and OpCo each amended their senior unsecured revolving credit agreements with Westlake, extending the maturities to July 2031.
quotes: These amendments extended the maturity dates of the facilities to July 2031.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited 8-K earnings release
material_events.claim: The board of the general partner approved a third-quarter 2026 distribution of $0.4714 per common unit, payable December 1, 2026. It is described as the 49th consecutive quarterly distribution.
quotes: On November 2, 2026, the Partnership announced that the Board of Directors of Westlake Chemical Partners GP LLC had approved a quarterly distribution for the third quarter of 2026 of $0.4714 per common unit to be payable on December 1, 2026 to unitholders of record as of November 13, 2026, representing the 49th consecutive quarterly distribution to our unitholders.

material_events.claim: OpCo and Westlake renewed the Ethylene Sales Agreement, and also the Feedstock Supply Agreement, through December 31, 2027. This is a renewal, not a loss of the contract.
quotes: On October 28, 2025, OpCo and Westlake agreed to renew the Ethylene Sales Agreement through December 31, 2027 in accordance with its terms.

material_events.claim: Tommy E. Darby was appointed Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer of the general partner, succeeding Jeffrey A. Holy, who moves to Vice President, Finance and Investor Relations.
quotes: Mr. Darby will succeed Jeffrey A. Holy, who will transition from his current position of Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer of the General Partner to the position of Vice President, Finance and Investor Relations of the General Partner, effective concurrent with the appointment of Mr. Darby.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and business sections (P1, P2, P3); the mechanism is inferred from them.
risks.claim: The Ethylene Sales Agreement, Feedstock Supply Agreement and Services and Secondment Agreement are the core of OpCo's cash flow, and the filing states that a failure to extend or replace them in future would hurt distributions. They were renewed past their initial term, but the renewal does not remove the dependence.
quotes: If OpCo were unable to reach agreement with Westlake on an extension or replacement of these agreements in the future, then our ability to make distributions on our common units could be materially adversely affected and the value of our common units could decline.

risks.basis: Risk wording stated in P2; balances stated in F1 and F3; the link between the two is inferred.
risks.claim: Westlake is the main customer, supplier, service provider and lender, and it has pledged no security. The partnership also lends it cash under the Investment Management Agreement: the receivable was 65,715 (table in thousands) against 23,378 (table in thousands) at year-end 2025, after investments of 42,000 (table in thousands) in the nine months.
quotes: Westlake has not pledged any assets to us as security for the performance of its obligations.

risks.basis: Coverage figures stated in P5 and P8; the sensitivity to a weaker quarter is inferred.
risks.claim: Distribution coverage is thin and the distribution is discretionary. Trailing twelve-month coverage was 1.09x, up from 1.04x at the end of Q2 and 1.00x at the end of Q1, so a weaker quarter could push coverage back toward or below the declared distribution.
quotes: MLP distributable cash flow provided trailing twelve-month coverage that was 1.09x the declared distributions for the third quarter of 2026, which was above the trailing twelve-month coverage ratio of 1.04x at the end of the second quarter.
The board of directors may modify or revoke our cash distribution policy at any time at its discretion.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 and P3; the mechanism and comparison are inferred.
risks.claim: Earnings depend on three ethylene facilities at two sites. The 2025 Petro 1 turnaround lowered 2025 MLP distributable cash flow to 53,398 (table in thousands) from 66,864 (table in thousands), showing how an outage or turnaround overrun can hit distributable cash.
quotes: Substantially all of OpCo's sales are generated at three facilities located at two sites.
In January 2025, we commenced our planned maintenance turnaround of the Petro 1 production facility.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 and P3 and in the income statement (F2); the mechanism for the 2025 margin decline is management's, not independently verified.
risks.claim: The fixed $0.10 per pound margin does not cover the partnership's own debt and public-company costs, and it limits upside. The 2025 gross margin fell to 29.8% from 36.9%, which management attributed to higher ethane and natural gas costs.
quotes: The ethylene sales price also does not increase to cover our cost of debt or public partnership costs.
The decreased gross profit margin in 2025 was primarily due to higher ethane feedstock and natural gas costs in 2025 as compared to 2024.

risks.basis: Stated in P2, P4, F1 and F3; the effect of rate changes is inferred.
risks.claim: The partnership carries 399,674 (table in thousands) of long-term debt payable to Westlake on variable-rate facilities. The filing flags interest-rate exposure, though revolver maturities were extended and the nine-month revolver draws and repayments were equal.
quotes: Our variable-rate debt exposes us to increases in interest rates, which could have a material impact on our financial position, results of operation and cash flows, and could reduce the price at which our common units trade.

risks.basis: Stated in the risk factor summary (P2); the income statement figure is from F2; the link is inferred.
risks.claim: The partnership's tax treatment depends on keeping partnership status for federal income tax. Loss of that status or a legislative change would create entity-level tax and reduce cash available for distribution.
quotes: Our tax treatment depends on our status as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and not being subject to a material amount of entity-level taxation.

unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the rise in nine-month operating cash flow to 362,205 (table in thousands) from 160,090 (table in thousands) comes from working-capital and turnaround-spend timing, and how much is recurring?

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the statement of operations and releases; the price/volume split for the quarter is not in the packet

quotes: The Applicable Margin under the OpCo Revolver is 1.75%.

quotes: In January 2025, we commenced our planned maintenance turnaround of the Petro 1 production facility.
